status: DRAFT 2026-10-16 rev 2 - accepted spellings tightened after review; owner sign-off on Korean still pending
about: Content for the Sejong Test playable slice (Batches 0-1). Batch/letter choice follows docs/sejong-test-spec.md v2. Voice follows the Hangul Tutor Voice Guide. 'source' marks historical facts (haerye = Hunminjeongeum Haerye, 1446) versus invented narrator lines.

wager.scope: 24 basic letters plus simple consonant-vowel blocks; no batchim
wager.timer: active play only; pauses when hidden or after 120 s without input

letters.shape: Your tongue tip touching the ridge behind your top teeth. Say 'n' and feel it.

letters.sound: a soft d, between the d in 'do' and the t in 'stop'
letters.shape: ㄴ with a lid on top. One more stroke, a firmer sound.

notice_line.speaker: jeong
notice_line.text: His Majesty preferred a system to a collection.

letters.shape: A standing person, with the sky's dot on the right.

letters.sound: o, as in 'go' (without the w at the end)
letters.shape: The flat earth, with the sky's dot above it.

confusion_pairs.tell: ㄷ has the extra stroke on top.
ㅏ's short stroke points right. ㅗ's points up.

first_read_line.speaker: jeong
first_read_line.text: Do, as in do-re-mi. A musical education, at no extra charge.

first_read_line.speaker: jeong
first_read_line.text: "Me too." Two syllables, and you can already agree with people.

letters.shape: The shape of a mouth. Close your lips: 'm'.

letters.sound: a soft b, between the b in 'bus' and the p in 'spin'
letters.shape: ㅁ with two strokes added. Lips again, with a small burst.
ㅏ turned around: the dot is on the left now.
ㅗ upside down: the dot is below the earth.

confusion_pairs.tell: ㅂ has two strokes sticking up.
Check which side the short stroke is on.
Up is ㅗ. Down is ㅜ.

first_read_line.speaker: jeong
first_read_line.text: "Tofu." You can now read a menu. Partially.

first_read_line.speaker: jeong
first_read_line.text: "Everyone." Which is exactly who these letters were for.

first_read_line.speaker: jeong
first_read_line.text: "Parents." A useful word. Their advice is usually longer.

first_read_line.speaker: jeong
first_read_line.text: "You," casually. Do not say it to your elders. Or to me.

first_read_line.speaker: jeong
first_read_line.text: "Too" or "very." Even excess has its uses.

words.en: two (before a noun or counter, as in 'two of them'; counting on its own is 둘)

first_read_line.speaker: jeong
first_read_line.text: "Two," before a noun or counter. For counting on its own: 둘. Korean has opinions about counting.

intro.speaker: sejong
intro.text: My people could not write their own words. So I made twenty-eight letters, for everyone.

intro.speaker: jeong
intro.text: Some learned gentlemen objected. They had spent rather a long time becoming learned gentlemen.

intro.speaker: jeong
intro.text: I wrote that a wise person learns these letters in a morning, and a fool in ten days.

intro.speaker: jeong
intro.text: A confident claim. Let us find out how confidently I should have written it.

intro.speaker: jeong
intro.text: Twenty-four of His Majesty's letters are still in use today. Those are your test.

0.speaker: jeong
0.text: Four letters. Two consonants, two vowels. That is enough to begin.

1.speaker: jeong
1.text: Four more. Each one looks like a letter you already know. That is not an accident.

predict_prompt.speaker: jeong
predict_prompt.text: You know {consonant} and you know {vowel}. Put them together. Which block do they make?

0.speaker: jeong
0.text: 나. It means 'I'. You have just written yourself.

1.speaker: jeong
1.text: 무. A radish. Not glamorous, but entirely yours.

first_breakthrough.speaker: jeong
first_breakthrough.text: Four letters, and you can build syllables. My colleagues would be alarmed.

5.speaker: jeong
5.text: Five in a row. The morning is looking possible.

10.speaker: jeong
10.text: Ten in a row. My reputation thanks you.

15.speaker: jeong
15.text: Fifteen. I shall take some credit for the instruction.

repeated_miss.speaker: jeong
repeated_miss.text: Then my explanation needs improvement. Look again.

repeated_miss.speaker: jeong
repeated_miss.text: My fault. Look closer this time.

first_word_read.speaker: jeong
first_word_read.text: You read it without me. Most inconvenient for my importance.

fool_word.speaker: jeong
fool_word.text: 바보. 'Fool.' Reading it does not make you one. Taking ten days might.
fool_word.playtest_alt: 바보. 'Fool.' Merely reading the word proves nothing. We shall reserve judgment.

decode_check_intro.speaker: jeong
decode_check_intro.text: Now, no choices. Read these yourself. Four out of five, and I will call it reading.

decode_check_fail.speaker: jeong
decode_check_fail.text: Not yet. We practice the ones you missed, then try again. The clock is patient. Mostly.

victory_1.speaker: sejong
victory_1.text: Now you can read your first words.

hour.speaker: jeong
hour.text: At this pace, all twenty-four before the hour is out. I may have been modest.

morning.speaker: jeong
morning.text: At this pace, done before the morning ends. As I wrote.

ten_days.speaker: jeong
ten_days.text: At this pace, ten days. The fool's pace, and still faster than any yangban learned his first hundred Chinese characters.

longer.speaker: jeong
longer.text: Slower than I promised. Then I miscounted. You are reading anyway, and that was the point.

victory_2.speaker: jeong
victory_2.text: Twenty-four basic letters. And you have already put them to use.
victory_2.use: Victory 2: let the learner enjoy finishing before any reveal.

complexity_reveal.speaker: jeong
complexity_reveal.text: I said you would learn the letters in a morning. I never said Korean.
complexity_reveal.use: Right after Victory 2, before the next layer (spec 7.7).

dodo_word.speaker: jeong
dodo_word.text: 도도. 'Haughty.' A word my colleagues never needed to read. They only needed to be it.

return_after_pause.speaker: jeong
return_after_pause.text: Welcome back. The clock stopped while you were away. I am more patient than I look.

resume_saved.speaker: jeong
resume_saved.text: Your place is saved. Shall we resume?

decode_check_pass.speaker: jeong
decode_check_pass.text: Four of five. You can read these. My claim survives another examination.

side.speaker: jeong
side.text: Close. A tall vowel like {vowel} stands beside the consonant.

stack.speaker: jeong
stack.text: Close. A flat vowel like {vowel} sits underneath the consonant.

before_show.speaker: jeong
before_show.text: Can you read this? No? Good. Remember that.

after_right.speaker: jeong
after_right.text: A little while ago, that was a squiggle.

after_close.speaker: jeong
after_close.text: Close. It reads {roman}: "{en}." A little while ago, that was a squiggle.

baseline_offer.speaker: jeong
baseline_offer.text: First, how much can you read already? Eight quick questions. Guess freely. Or skip, if you are confident there is nothing to measure.
baseline_offer.deprecated: Remove after the before/after change is merged.

baseline_skip.speaker: jeong
baseline_skip.text: Skipping the test. Confident, or cautious? We shall see.
baseline_skip.deprecated: Remove after the before/after change is merged.

baseline_zero.speaker: jeong
baseline_zero.text: Then we begin at the beginning. A perfectly respectable place.
baseline_zero.deprecated: Remove after the before/after change is merged.

accepted_rule: Grading uses the engine's roman_variants() only; this file does not add spellings. Engine today: ㅓ = eo only; ㅜ = u or oo; ㄷ/ㅂ = d/b only; ㅏ/ㅗ = a/o only. No alias is shared between two letters taught together.

later_words.note: Owner-suggested everyday words for later batches (batch per sejong-test-spec letter order).

humor_rules: Jokes target words, history, the elite scholars, or Jeong himself; never the learner's mistakes. Miss feedback stays plain.
A word's first_read_line is eligible on its first reading only; words without one show the meaning plainly.
'Show-off' is reserved for a perfect decode check.
notice_line is a visual observation; the 'shape' field is the historical (Haerye) account. Keep them distinct.
return_after_pause is only true because the timer stops when the page is hidden or idle over 120 s.

before_after.note: Shown unscored right after the intro; asked again (typed) just before Victory 1. Replaces the 8-question baseline and post-test.
